_comment: Tier-2 prompt evals: real model, scored, on demand only. Never wired into CI. See docs/prompt-evals.md.

judge._source: Copied from close_verification_prompt in crates/openhuman-core/src/agent/session_host/turn_checkpoint.rs (pub(super), deliberately not widened for this script). The Rust copy has a drift guard; if you edit the rules there, mirror them here.
judge.preamble: You are checking a reply before it is shown to a user. Below are the user's request, the records of the tool calls made while handling it, and the reply.
rules: The reply only says what the assistant will do or is about to do, instead of reporting what happened.

The reply states something the tool records contradict, for example that something does not exist or did not work when a record shows it succeeded, or that something succeeded when its record shows it failed.
The request was not completed, a failed record gives the reason, and the reply does not pass that reason on.

cases._why: Direct-first: a single current fact is one built-in web_search_tool call, not a research spawn.
cases.message: What is the latest stable release of the Rust programming language? Cite where you found it.

cases._why: ERROR-PATH case, not an MCP capability case: the account has zero MCP servers, so the only honest outcome is to say none is configured without fabricating one or installing one. Do not install a server to make MCP testable — that changes the baseline.
cases.message: Use my MCP server to look up today's open tickets.

cases._why: Direct-first: a trivial question must be answered without spawning a sub-agent.
Run an installed skill through its hand-off, read-only. The account's only installed skill on 2026-09-18 was `notion` (it was `github` two days earlier — re-check).
cases.message: Using my installed Notion skill, list the titles of my five most recently edited Notion pages. Do not create or edit anything.
cases._precondition_finding: skills_list defaults include_skills=false and then lists only workflows/ automations (skills/schemas/handlers.rs:32, #3954), so an installed skill is hidden; include_skills=true also reads skills/ roots. The response key is 'workflows' for both (legacy naming), while skills_schemas('skills_list') declares the output as 'skills'. A schema-driven caller, agent included, is misled the same way.

cases._why: The 2026-09-17 incident: 512,775 input tokens and 27 catalog searches in one turn, no propose_workflow.
cases.message: Every morning at 8am, send me a digest of the latest sports news.
cases._writes_note: flows_build proposes only; nothing is saved unless the model calls save_workflow/create_workflow (forbidden below).

cases._why: Integration hand-off to a connected toolkit, read-only. Exercises delegate_to_integrations_agent and the text-mode integrations_agent (see #6334).
cases.message: What is the subject line of the most recent email in my Gmail inbox? Just read it, don't change anything.
cases._gate: Do not run until a real transcript has shown a text-mode integrations_agent call in `calls` in a form these forbids match. Until then GMAIL_* forbids are unproven against the live inbox.

cases._why: A scheduling request must reach scheduler_agent through schedule_task, not be answered in prose.
cases.message: Remind me to stretch every weekday at 3pm.
writes: a recurring cron job ('stretch', weekdays 15:00) — remove it with cron_remove / the Routines UI after the run

_precondition_note: precondition: a read-only RPC run just before each run. expect_regex must match / expect_not_regex must not match its JSON output. The regexes are UNVERIFIED against real output: inspect `precondition.evidence` in the first rows. A failed precondition skips the run and records why.
_order: Cases run in file order: increasing account risk. Nothing-touching cases first (they also validate the rig), the one writing case last.
